cells.tense: Right now the mix is open in front of you and you are stirring it by feel.
cells.act: teach it the way it was taught to you, with one change
cells.ask: Show somebody how you do something you're good at, the way it was shown to you, with one part altered to suit you. One sitting is enough.
cells.core:
You can watch a thing work under the surface and correct as it goes — a little more of this, less of that, until it runs. That isn't stiffness and it isn't luck. When it's going well, the shape holds even while the pieces move, and nobody standing next to you has to hold it too. What bends it now is thinking the shape needs explaining. It doesn't. The auditing is running while the mix is already right, and the checking costs more than the adjusting did.

So pass something on. Take a skill of yours and show it to somebody the way it was shown to you, changing one part to make it yours. The old form keeps its bones and picks up your hand. What remains is not a copy and not a replacement — the same thing living on with you inside it, and somebody else able to run it without you watching.

cells.tense: You are already smoothing the next blowup before anyone has said anything out loud.
cells.ask: Take a step toward something you actually want, today, before the ground feels even under it. No announcement first. Let the step after this one stay unwritten for now.
cells.core:
Where the mixing gets done, differences are being flattened before anyone has to feel them. You sense a small disagreement forming and you're blending the edges already, so the sentence that needed saying goes unsaid and stays where it was spoken. Harmony this early works like a muzzle. The people beside you can hear the hush, and it doesn't register as peace to them.

Direction comes back through wanting, not through adjusting. Move toward something you actually want — today, before it feels level — a step, no announcement, no fixing the mood first. A choice made from what you want carries differently than a choice made to keep things calm, and the difference turns up in your shoulders before it turns up anywhere you could point to.

cells.tense: You were scattered by the last thing that reached you and you are still standing in that hallway.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Next time someone near you is having a hard time, stay with them and fix nothing — no advice, no smoothing, no hurrying out. Sit there while it's bad, keeping your own footing.
cells.core:
Where the mix gets made, no steady hand is on it now. Whatever the room is doing, you're doing, and by evening there's little you'd call your own. The pattern is still there to be seen and you get carried past it before you can look. This isn't coldness. Whatever you had in reserve went somewhere, and the next stretch will ask for more than is left.

Steadiness comes back by way of somebody else's trouble, not your own. When someone near you is struggling, sit with them and fix nothing — no advice, no smoothing, no exiting early. Stay while it's hard and hold your own side of it. You'll find your middle by feeling alongside theirs, which is how it tends to get found.

cells.tense: You are running the adjustment all day and the story you tell is that you don't.
cells.act: learn how the people before you did it
cells.ask: Trace a practice of yours back — ask whoever did it before you, or read an old account of it. Find out whose hands it passed through.
cells.core:
The tuning happens constantly and goes unowned. You sense what a group needs and shift toward it, then say you're easygoing; you find the shape of a problem and call it obvious. The skill is real and its author is missing. Anyone watching would not describe you as passive. They watch you land in the right register in three seconds flat.

Trace what you carry to its source, then. Learn how a practice of yours was done before you — ask whoever did it, or read an old account of it. One lineage is enough. When you can name whose hands it came through, the adjustments stop looking like something that happened to you and start looking like something you did.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that this person was ever taught or shown the pattern in the first place — the record gives a channel and a house, not a history, so the Too Little cell says only where they stand and what the absence looks like now, never who or when. A reader could reasonably say the pattern-seeing is going fine and the problem is elsewhere; if so, the asks still hold, because each one is a single small act with no payoff promised and no condition attached. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the phrase about the rhythm being steady enough to trust — cut it, since nothing in the person's life has been shown to be steady, and the cell would be praising its own instrument.
